props.title: Dreamgirls
props.initialSlug: Rising Motown singers chase stardom & betrayal

sections.content: **Dreamgirls** (2006) revolutionized the modern movie musical with powerhouse performances and a raw look at the 1960s music industry. Jennifer Hudson's Oscar-winning turn as Effie White follows the tradition of breakthrough musical performances like Barbra Streisand in **Funny Girl** (1968). The film's exploration of the Motown era draws clear parallels to The Supremes' rise, while director Bill Condon brings the same dramatic intensity he delivered in **Chicago** (2002). The "And I Am Telling You I'm Not Going" sequence stands as one of cinema's most electrifying musical moments.

sections.content: The film sits at a crucial intersection between Hollywood musicals and African American cultural representation. While earlier films like **Carmen Jones** (1954) broke ground for Black performers in movie musicals, **Dreamgirls** captures both the glory and exploitation of the 1960s music industry. The transition from raw R&B to polished pop mirrors similar themes in **What's Love Got to Do with It** (1993) and **Ray** (2004), examining how Black artists navigated a white-controlled industry.

Musical staging in **Dreamgirls** marked a departure from the theatrical approach of films like **Moulin Rouge!** (2001). Condon grounds musical numbers in realistic settings while maintaining their emotional impact. The rehearsal scenes and recording studio sequences feel authentic to the era, while showstopping numbers like "One Night Only" blend stage spectacle with cinematic sweep. This balance influenced later musicals like **La La Land** (2016). SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Movie Musicals

sections.content: **Dreamgirls** bridges classic Hollywood musicals and contemporary film adaptations. Its success paved the way for more ambitious projects like **Les Misérables** (2012) and **Into the Woods** (2014). The film's emphasis on live singing, particularly in Hudson's dramatic moments, influenced later productions to favor authentic vocal performances over studio perfection. This trend reached its apex with **A Star Is Born** (2018).
